subject.title: perf(sqlite): fast schema gates, background integrity verification, and downgrade protection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt persistent daily database quarantine and fail-closed schema gates as the core downgrade and corruption-recovery policy for existing installations?
rationale: This is more than a local performance repair: it establishes a persistent state model and deliberately changes startup, updater, and recovery behavior for existing databases.

options.title: Adopt with upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the core approach after redacted real-world proof covers managed-service update refusal, gateway preflight, and successful doctor recovery.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Land only the cheap schema gate and updater preflight, leaving persistent daily verification and quarantine for a separately approved design.

options.title: Pause for storage-policy review
options.body: Defer the PR until owners decide whether derived quarantine state may be added without a state-schema version increment.

recommendation.title: Adopt with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the core approach after redacted real-world proof covers managed-service update refusal, gateway preflight, and successful doctor recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged SQLite safety work and this branch place them closest to the intended storage and recovery policy.
